title: Provider-neutral decision questions for SubQ Snap 1.1 and TypeSafe Jev 1.14

api.answer_shape: answers.<name>.noul (probability of yes) | answers.<name>.{choice, confidence, probabilities} | answers.<name>.{score, confidence, probabilities}
api.limits: 1-16 named questions per request; 384K-token context; score questions take 2-10 ordered level descriptions; choice questions 2-255 options
api.verification_status: SECOND-HAND. docs.subq.ai was not reachable from the session that wrote this file; the shape follows the published quickstart as quoted by search results and two open-source clients (devbux/subq-snap-mcp, opentalon PR #394), and matches the TypeSafe System One shape already used in capstone/providers/typesafe.py. Confirm the exact key for score levels (criteria vs levels) against docs.subq.ai before the first live request.
api.note: `api` describes the Snap request as first written; `providers` is the authoritative per-provider table.

providers.rule: In a matched comparison both providers receive the same state fitted to 28,000 tokens by evaltools.decision_models.fit_state, the same named questions, criteria, scales and missing-evidence rules; answers are normalized by evaltools.decision_models.normalize and compared by evaltools.decision_models.compare. Both services' request shapes are second-hand (docs unreachable from the authoring session); see evaluation/DECISION_MODEL_COMPARISON.md for what to confirm.

principles: Deterministic checks take precedence: a question is never asked where code already computes the answer from the record or the hidden truth.
Snap judges the quality of the investigation, never whether the answer matches ground truth; the judge's state never carries the true fault.

Every question has a missing-evidence rule. A packet with trace.completeness = record_only cannot answer RUN-01, RUN-02, RUN-05, RUN-06, RUN-08, RUN-09, RUN-10 or RUN-12 (evaltools.snap_request.NEEDS_FULL_TRACE); those are recorded as 'unknown' without a request.
A probability from a noul question is a model's preference, not a calibrated correctness probability. Thresholds below are decision rules for the report, not claims about calibration.
Scores are reported per item and per batch with their denominators; nothing is folded into one overall percentage.

The judge sees each question's type, instructions and criteria, with its missing-evidence rule appended to the instructions (DecisionQuestion.to_request). Fields such as applies_to, deterministic_precedence, scoring_note and decision_rule are for the evaluator and reviewers; nothing a judge needs in order to answer may live only there.
Score levels are exclusive: each level says what separates it from the next, so one trace fits one level. Choice options are exclusive; where two could apply, the instructions say which one wins.
A reading counts wherever it appears in a trace. Phase names (observe, investigate, test) are the loop's bookkeeping, not part of what a reading shows.
Designed degradations (the hazards a run reports) are measured by the deterministic hazard checks, not by the judge; judge questions look for undesigned failures.

questions.name: evidence_quality
questions.instructions: Read `trace`. Judge whether the final `conclusion.diagnosis` is supported by relevant evidence the factory itself returned (origin 'observable'), rather than by assumptions, manual guidance or memory alone. Consider only evidence ids the conclusion or the selected hypothesis cites and what those items actually contain. A rival is any other cause the agent listed (hypotheses and pruned candidates) or the retrieved manual names for this symptom; a discriminating reading is one whose result would differ depending on which of the two is true. Readings count in any phase. When the conclusion names no single cause, judge the support for the causes it keeps open and the ones it rules out.
criteria: 0: The conclusion cites no observable evidence, or nothing it cites bears on the claim.
1: Cited observable evidence relates to the claim only loosely: a symptom the claim depends on was never read.
2: Cited observable evidence shows the symptom, but no reading separates the claim from any rival.
3: At least one discriminating reading separates the claim from a rival, but at least one rival is left unseparated.
4: Discriminating readings separate the claim from every rival, and other machines or batches were checked before the conclusion.
questions.missing_evidence: If trace.completeness is record_only, do not ask; record unknown.
questions.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.evidence_share and relevant_evidence_collected give the truth-side view of coverage; this question gives the judge's view of whether what was collected supports what was concluded. Report both, never one for the other.
questions.scoring_note: Report the probability-weighted score and the modal level; a mean below 2 on a run scored root_cause_correct=true is flagged 'misleading success'.

questions.name: hypothesis_reasoning
questions.instructions: Read `trace.hypotheses`, `trace.pruned_candidates` and every decision, in any phase. Judge whether the investigator considered competing plausible causes and tested them against each other, rather than pursuing one explanation from the start. A cause that needs no repair is a transient, a material batch, a setting, an instrument fault or normal operation. The kinds of cause the retrieved manual names for this symptom (for example operating change, transient, instrument, equipment, material) set what a complete set covers. Readings count in any phase.
criteria: 0: One hypothesis only, or several that are rewordings of the same cause.
1: Distinct hypotheses were listed, but no reading anywhere in the trace was aimed at telling them apart.

2: Distinct hypotheses and at least one reading that bears on a rival, but the confidences do not follow the readings: a confidence moved without a reading that bears on it, or the leading hypothesis kept its confidence after a reading that contradicts it.

3: Distinct hypotheses, readings that tell them apart and confidences that follow those readings, but the set missed a plausible cause: a kind of cause the retrieved manual names for this symptom, or any cause that needs no repair.

4: As 3, and the set covered the plausible causes: it held at least one cause that needs no repair, and every kind of cause the retrieved manual names for this symptom was listed or set aside with a stated reason.
questions.deterministic_precedence: none; this is interpretation. Testing done in the investigate phase counts the same as in the test phase.

questions.name: critic_effectiveness
questions.applies_to: one master-run packet with trace.critique present
questions.instructions: Read `trace.critique`, `trace.recheck`, the hypotheses and the conclusion. Did the critic identify an important weakness (a contradiction, a missing check, a better alternative) and did a useful follow-up happen when one was warranted? If the critic names a real weakness but its check tests something else, the answer is ineffective.

criteria.effective: The critic named a real weakness or the best-supported alternative, and its check (or the conclusion) addresses that weakness.
criteria.ineffective: The critic missed an evident weakness, objected without substance, named a check that cannot test its own point (one that repeats readings already in hand, or a window that ends after the current tick), or its point was ignored (recheck skipped, policy_stopped, or the conclusion unchanged despite a contradicting reading).
criteria.not_required: The leading hypothesis was already separated from every plausible rival and the critic's agreement was reasonable; no follow-up was needed.
criteria.unknown: No usable critique (outcome no_answer or invalid_reply), or the trace is incomplete.

questions.missing_evidence: No critique record: not asked; recorded as not_run.
questions.deterministic_precedence: critique.verdict_mismatch, recheck.outcome and recheck.trigger are code facts; evaluator_only.critic_pick_correct says whether the pick named the true cause. Those are reported beside this answer.

questions.name: retrieval_quality
questions.applies_to: one master-run packet with manual or memory offered
questions.instructions: Read `trace.manual_searches`, `trace.recall_searches`, the evidence items whose origin is 'manual' or 'memory', and the hypotheses, decisions and conclusion. Did the retrieved passages or memories materially support the investigation? Use counts whether or not the item is cited by id. If more than one option applies, choose in this order: misleading, ignored, useful.

criteria.useful: A retrieved passage shaped the investigation: it is cited by id, or a hypothesis, a decision or the conclusion uses a check, cause or caution that appears in the passage and not in the anomaly text, consistently with what the passage says.
criteria.ignored: The conclusion goes against a caution a retrieved passage states for this symptom, or skips the check a passage recommends for telling apart the causes the conclusion weighs, without saying why.
criteria.misleading: A retrieved passage was cited or followed in support of a claim it does not support, or steered a reading away from the symptom.
criteria.unnecessary: Retrieval answered, nothing retrieved was used, and nothing retrieved bore on the conclusion.
criteria.not_retrieved: The tool was offered but never answered a search (no search, or every search refused or failed).

questions.missing_evidence: Neither offered: not asked; recorded as not_offered.
questions.deterministic_precedence: search counts, refusals and the sections returned are code facts (manual_searches, recall_searches); whether a memory was cited is `memory_uses.used` in the record.

questions.name: verification_demonstrated
questions.instructions: Read `trace.verification`, `trace.proposal` and the evidence observed after `action_finish_tick` (or after the conclusion for a no-action run). Does the trace show that the agent checked its prediction against observations made after the work, and that the verdict follows from them?

criteria.yes: Observable evidence with a data window after the work (or after the conclusion) was read, the verdict cites it, and the cited values agree with the verdict.
criteria.no: No look after the work, the verdict cites evidence from before the work, or the cited values contradict the verdict.
criteria.not_applicable: The run ended with escalate or without a proposal, so no remedy was there to verify.

questions.deterministic_precedence: The loop already refuses a verdict that rests on evidence from before the work (`capstone.agent.investigation.verify`); evaluator_only.verification_calibration compares the verdict with the truth. This question adds only whether the cited numbers support the verdict.

questions.name: abstention_appropriate
questions.instructions: Read the conclusion, its assessment and recommendation, the hypotheses and the evidence. Decide whether the agent named a single cause, and whether the cited evidence justified that decision. A conclusion that names one cause counts as committed even when a later check lowered its recommendation to escalate; one that keeps two or more causes open, or names none, counts as declined. Judge the decision, not the confidence figure (RUN-09 judges the figure).

criteria.appropriate: Declined when the cited evidence left two or more causes open, or committed when cited readings separate the named cause from every plausible rival.
criteria.inappropriate: Declined although cited readings separate one cause from every plausible rival, or committed while a plausible rival was untested or a contradiction stood.
criteria.not_applicable: The run never reached a reasoned conclusion (model unavailable, undetermined by timeout).

questions.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.abstained and confident_wrong are code facts from the label and the truth; this question judges the decision against the evidence shown, not against the truth.

questions.name: failure_classification
questions.applies_to: one master-run packet; asked of every run, with none_observed for one that reads as sound, so the judge never learns from the question which runs were wrong
questions.instructions: Read the whole trace. What most seriously undermined this investigation? Choose the single earliest cause that, had it gone right, would most likely have changed the outcome. If the run reads as sound, choose none_observed.

criteria.reasoning: The readings needed were in hand and were misread: the hypotheses, confidences or conclusion do not follow from the cited evidence.
criteria.evidence_gathering: The agent stopped or concluded before making a reading that its own hypotheses or the retrieved manual called for, with no tool failure or budget forcing it.
criteria.retrieval: A manual or memory answer was absent, unhelpful or misleading at the point it mattered.
criteria.critic: The critic missed or misdirected, or its correct point was dropped.
criteria.tooling: Tool errors, refused calls, repeated calls, a blackout or a gap left the needed reading unavailable, or the time or call budget ran out while the agent was still collecting it.
criteria.verification: The diagnosis and action are supported by the trace, but the post-action check was missing or wrong.
criteria.none_observed: Nothing undermined it: the investigation reads as sound.

questions.missing_evidence: record_only packets: the judge may use tools_used, decisions outcomes and termination_reason only; answer unknown unless a tooling or timeout cause is evident from them.
questions.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.miss_kind (evidence_miss vs reasoning_miss) and facts.termination_reason are code facts reported beside this answer; evidence_gathering and reasoning are the judge's view of the same split.

questions.name: conclusion_support
questions.instructions: Independently of whether the diagnosis is true, how well does the trace support the final conclusion as stated? Consider every claim the conclusion states as settled, the unexplained and contradicting evidence the hypotheses list, the open questions, and whether the stated confidence matches. For a conclusion that keeps causes open, its claim is the set it keeps open and the set it rules out; open questions it states as open lower the score only when they undermine something it states as settled.
criteria: 0: Not supported: the cited evidence is absent, irrelevant or contradicts the conclusion.
1: Weakly supported: one consistent reading, with the alternatives or contradictions left open.
2: Partly supported: the symptom is shown, but a claim the conclusion states as settled is not supported by the cited evidence, or an open question it lists undermines one of its own settled claims.

3: Well supported: every claim stated as settled is supported by the cited evidence and the named cause (or the causes kept open) is separated from the alternatives the agent considered, but the stated confidence is out of proportion or something material is left open.
4: Fully supported: as 3, with the confidence proportionate and nothing material left open.
questions.deterministic_precedence: `check_conclusion` already lowers an unresolved conclusion to escalate; this question measures the quality of the text and citations, which code cannot.

questions.name: unsupported_confidence
questions.applies_to: one master-run packet whose conclusion names a cause (facts.committed), whatever its final recommendation
questions.instructions: Is the confidence in `trace.conclusion.confidence` higher than the cited evidence allows? This applies to any conclusion that names a cause, even when a later check lowered its recommendation to escalate. A rival is any other cause the agent listed (hypotheses and pruned candidates) or the retrieved manual names for this symptom; a discriminating reading is one whose result would differ depending on which of the two is true. Readings count in any phase.

criteria.true: Confidence is 0.8 or more while a rival was never separated by a reading, a contradiction or unexplained item is listed for the selected hypothesis, the conclusion's own unresolved questions leave the named cause open, or the cited evidence is a single reading.
criteria.false: Confidence is below 0.8, or it is 0.8 or more with every rival separated and nothing material left open.

questions.decision_rule: A probability of 0.7 or more is reported as 'overconfident'; 0.3 or less as 'proportionate'; between, 'unclear' (the TypeSafe thresholds already used by auto_label.py, not calibrated for this project).

questions.name: scan_before_no_fault
questions.applies_to: one master-run packet whose recommendation is no_action
questions.instructions: The conclusion says nothing needs fixing. Before concluding that, did the investigation examine machines other than the one the alarm named (list_machines, then readings or inspections for them)?

criteria.true: At least one other machine's sensor readings or the line's inspection results were read after the alarm and before the conclusion.
criteria.false: Only the alarmed machine was examined, or no machine list was read.

questions.deterministic_precedence: PREFER THE CODE: facts.machines_examined lists the machines named in tool arguments; with a full trace this question is redundant and is only asked to validate the deterministic check on the reference set.

questions.name: critic_feedback_used
questions.applies_to: one master-run packet with trace.critique and trace.recheck present
questions.instructions: Read `trace.critique` (the check it named), `trace.recheck` and the hypotheses before and after. Did the investigator use the critic's feedback?

criteria.used: The follow-up reading was made where the critic pointed, and the leading hypothesis or its confidence changed in the direction the reading supports, or stayed when the reading confirmed it.
criteria.ignored: A usable check was named and the follow-up was skipped, stopped by the policy or refused, or it was made but the beliefs did not respond to what it showed.
criteria.no_feedback: The critic gave no usable check: no_answer, invalid_reply, an empty discriminating_check, or a check that could not be carried out when it was given (for example a window that ends after the current tick).

questions.missing_evidence: No recheck record: not asked (the follow-up was off).
questions.deterministic_precedence: recheck.outcome, confidence_before and confidence_after are code facts; this question adds whether the response to the reading was sensible.

questions.name: evidence_cited_matches_content
questions.instructions: For each evidence id the conclusion cites, read that item's content. Does every cited item actually show what the conclusion says it shows? Judge what each item contains, not whether the conclusion's inference from it is sound (RUN-08 judges that). A figure counts as shown when it matches the item to the precision the conclusion states.

criteria.true: Every cited item contains the reading, event or result the conclusion attributes to it.
criteria.false: At least one cited item does not contain what is attributed to it (wrong machine, wrong sensor, a value not present, an event not there, a time window that does not match), or the conclusion cites nothing.

questions.deterministic_precedence: `check_conclusion` verifies that cited ids exist and `verify_numeric_claims` checks structured numbers; neither checks the prose. This question covers the prose.

questions.name: implementation_matches_contract
questions.applies_to: one function evidence packet (source, docstring, variable block, tests)
questions.instructions: Read the function's source and its stated contract: the docstring and `# Variables:` block, and for a command-line `main` also its argparse description and help texts. Does the implementation do what the contract says, for every branch, including error paths? A return value, exit code or early exit the contract does not mention counts as undocumented behaviour a caller would need to know.

criteria.true: Every statement in the contract is implemented and no branch does something the contract does not describe.
criteria.false: A documented behaviour is missing, a branch does something undocumented that a caller would need to know, or the contract is absent so nothing can be matched.

questions.missing_evidence: No docstring and no variable block: answer false and flag 'contract unspecified'.
questions.deterministic_precedence: Test outcomes (passed/failed) are code facts from the junit report.

questions.name: failure_paths_covered
questions.instructions: Compare the function's branches, raises and except clauses with the tests listed as executing it. Are the failure and boundary paths exercised by a test that asserts on their outcome?

criteria.covered: Every raise, except clause, error exit or return code, and boundary branch (an optional argument absent, an empty collection) visible in the source is reached by a listed test that asserts on its outcome.
criteria.partly: The happy path and at least one of those are asserted; at least one is not.
criteria.uncovered: Only the happy path is asserted, or the listed tests execute the function without asserting on its result.
criteria.not_applicable: The function has no failure or boundary branch (pure data access, a property).

questions.deterministic_precedence: Line coverage and the test list are code facts from the verification matrix; the judge rates the assertions.

questions.name: evidence_sufficient_for_correctness
questions.instructions: Given the tests that execute this function, their assertions and their outcomes, is the available evidence sufficient to call the function correct against its contract?

criteria.sufficient: Direct tests assert the contract's behaviour on realistic inputs, including failure paths and every outcome the contract states, and all passed.
criteria.insufficient: The function is executed only incidentally by other tests, assertions are weak, a failure path or an outcome the contract states is untested, or a test failed or was skipped.
criteria.not_applicable: A stub, a protocol method or a one-line accessor whose correctness is established by its type alone.

questions.deterministic_precedence: The verification matrix's coverage_class is the starting point; the judge may lower but never raise a FAILED or NOT TESTED status.

questions.name: test_proves_its_claim
questions.applies_to: one test evidence packet (test source, docstring, functions exercised, outcome)
questions.instructions: The test's name and docstring make a claim. Do its assertions establish that claim about the project code it exercises? `decorators` holds the test's decorators (for example its parametrize values) and `module_helpers` the source of helper functions from the test's module that it calls or takes as fixtures.

criteria.true: The assertions check the specific behaviour the name claims, on inputs that exercise it.
criteria.false: The assertions check something weaker or different from the claim (only that no error occurred, only a type, only a field exists), or the claim is not about project code.

questions.missing_evidence: If no project function is listed as exercised, judge the project classes or modules the test constructs, calls or imports (validation declared on a project model counts as project code); answer false only if it exercises no project code at all.
questions.deterministic_precedence: assertion counts and forms are code facts.

questions.name: would_fail_if_broken
questions.instructions: Imagine the behaviour the test claims to verify were broken in the implementation (the wrong branch taken, the check removed, the value off by one). Would this test fail? `module_helpers` shows what the helpers it uses do.

criteria.true: A plausible breakage of the claimed behaviour changes an asserted value.
criteria.false: The test could still pass because its inputs come from a stub that fixes the outcome, the assertion is on a mocked return, or the assertion is too loose to notice.

questions.deterministic_precedence: A mutation-testing result, where available, takes precedence over this judgement.

questions.name: assertion_strength
questions.instructions: Rate the specificity of the test's assertions relative to the behaviour it claims.
criteria: 0: No assertion, or only that no exception was raised.
1: Truthiness or not-None checks only.
2: Specific values or types asserted on part of the outcome; side effects or state transitions not checked where they matter.
3: Specific values asserted on the whole relevant outcome, including state changes or raised errors where the claim needs them.
questions.deterministic_precedence: quality_flags no_assertion and weak_assertions_only are code facts and fix the score at 0 or 1 without asking.

questions.name: boundary_enforced
questions.applies_to: one tool evidence packet (schema, implementation, provider wiring, tests)
questions.instructions: Read the tool's implementation and the provider's wiring. Can the tool return anything the agent must not see (hidden condition, ground truth, approval powers, raw errors with secrets), or change the factory without the intended authorization?

criteria.true: Every field returned is rebuilt from an output contract, no hidden field or secret can pass, and any factory change goes through the approval desk or the wait tool as designed. A note that reports what a person would observe by design (a technician's finding on a removed part) is evidence, not hidden state.
criteria.false: A code path can return hidden state, a raw exception, or change the factory without approval.

questions.deterministic_precedence: tests/test_observation_tools.py::test_nothing_hidden_leaks_through_any_tool_over_a_full_run and tests/test_factory_provider.py are the deterministic checks; this question looks for paths those tests do not reach.

questions.name: description_matches_behaviour
questions.instructions: Compare the tool description a model is shown with what the implementation does and refuses. Would a model that trusts the description be misled? A limit counts against the description only if a normal call can reach it.

criteria.true: The description states the arguments, limits and meaning of the answer as implemented.
criteria.false: The description promises something the implementation does not do, omits a limit the implementation enforces (rows, ranges, sensors), or describes the answer's meaning wrongly.

questions.deterministic_precedence: tests/test_factory_provider.py::test_every_tool_is_described_and_no_description_names_a_missing_tool checks presence, not accuracy.

questions.name: silent_failure_risk
questions.instructions: How likely is this tool to return a value that is wrong or incomplete without signalling failure (success=true with misleading data)? Designed degradations (the hazards in `hazards_note`, which runs report) do not count; judge undesigned ways the answer could be wrong or incomplete.
criteria: 0: Cannot: the answer is a direct projection of recorded data with no filtering that could drop rows.
1: Unlikely: filtering or arithmetic exists but is simple and tested on boundaries.
2: Possible: windows, units or ordering could silently exclude or distort data and the tests do not cover that case.
3: Likely: outside the designed hazards, the answer depends on state the agent cannot see (an unsynchronised cache, a source that may be incomplete) and nothing marks the answer as degraded.
questions.deterministic_precedence: The hazard tests pin the designed degradations; this question looks for undesigned ones.

questions.name: comparison_valid
questions.applies_to: one experiment comparison packet (two batch summaries with their configurations)
questions.instructions: Two batches are compared. From their configurations, commits, scenario sets, models, retrieval settings, rubric versions and label sources, is a like-for-like comparison valid?

criteria.valid: Same scenarios and seeds (or the same case hash), the same commit, label sources and rubric version, and exactly one configuration setting differs (the treatment); no run was resumed with different settings. Which model answered, outages and timing are outcomes, not configuration differences.
criteria.partially_valid: Same scenarios, but more than one configuration setting differs, or a resumed run changed settings partway, so a difference can be reported but not attributed.
criteria.invalid: Different scenarios, different label rules or rubric versions, or results of unknown configuration.

questions.deterministic_precedence: `capstone.evals.compare_reports` refuses different scenario sets; the rest is interpretation.

questions.name: improvement_supported
questions.instructions: Given the per-case results and the number of cases, does the evidence support a claim that the treatment improved root-cause accuracy and evidence-grounded decisions without more unsupported conclusions, more tool calls or more failures? A matched case is one judged in both batches; `sample_rule_in_code.matched_judged` counts them and `sample_rule_in_code.rule` applies the sample condition.

criteria.improvement: More cases right, no more confident-wrong, no more false interventions, and tool calls or latency not materially higher, over at least two repeats per case or 13 or more matched cases.
criteria.regression: Fewer right, or more confident-wrong or false interventions, with the same sample conditions.
criteria.no_difference: Differences within one case either way with the sample conditions met.
criteria.insufficient_sample: The sample conditions are not met: one run per case and fewer than 13 matched cases, or an outage hit a matched case on one side only.

questions.deterministic_precedence: All counts come from BATCH_SUMMARY.json; the judge applies the sample rule, which the report also applies in code.

changelog: 1.1.0 (2026-11-08): calibration round 1 found answers that depended on wording rather than evidence. Changed in meaning: RUN-01, RUN-02 and RUN-08 (exclusive levels), RUN-04 (new option ignored), RUN-06 (no confidence threshold; a check-lowered escalate still counts as committed), RUN-07 (new option evidence_gathering), RUN-09 (asked of every conclusion that names a cause; rivals and open questions spelled out), RUN-11 (a check that cannot be carried out is no_feedback), TS-01 (declarative project code counts), TL-03 (designed hazards excluded). Clarified without a change of meaning: RUN-03, RUN-12, FN-01, FN-02, FN-03, TS-02, TL-01, TL-02, BT-01, BT-02. Answers given under 1.0.0 are not comparable for the changed questions.
